reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free assignment right to Affiliates and M&A successors (notice only), matching the preferred position.

24.2 restricts Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance and transfer by change of control to Customer's prior written consent (reasonableness-qualified) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor; 24.3 supplies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld standard for other assignments.

24.4 expressly denies Vendor any termination, suspension, repricing, fee-acceleration or service-reduction right on Customer's change of control, eliminating the walk-away trigger; 13.3 aligns licence transfer with permitted Section 24 assignments.
No deemed-assignment trap or Vendor change-of-control exit was identified elsewhere, and the rationale correctly notes the mutual insolvency right in 9.2 carves out lawful reorganizations.

Consistent with a compliant finding, the redline is unchanged from the original paragraphs and no counterparty comment was proposed; the deterministic check for the successor/affiliate carve-out passes.
